recommendation: Keep the no-change audit as-is. Any future wording about informationProvider/sender terminology should be handled as a separate current-spec editorial or work-group decision, not as remaining work for FHIR-14959.
issue_request: FHIR-14959 was a Published Patient Care change request for STU3 asking to clarify the difference between requester and sender in CommunicationRequest. The final Not Persuasive with Modification resolution accepted adding the sentence that the requester requests the sender to send the payload to the recipient, and explicitly declined notes about what to do when requester and sender are the same.
initial_application: Commit 722ed5c93f4bc9828e96f0f5b476bedc3486fb92 applied GF#14959 by adding the accepted sentence to source/communicationrequest/communicationrequest-introduction.xml. No same requester/sender prohibition was added, matching the Jira comments and resolution.
additional_context: CommunicationRequest is active in source/fhir.ini. Later CommunicationRequest introduction changes, including J#46539/J#46540, J#46333, and J#51696, edited nearby wording and examples without removing or contradicting the FHIR-14959 sentence. Current element naming has evolved from the older sender element to informationProvider as the source of the communication, but the Scope and Usage sentence remains a generic sender/source explanation and does not create the declined same-party rule.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current active source already has the approved clarification: "The requester requests the sender to send the payload to the recipient." Source searches did not find the declined instruction to avoid using sender when requester and sender are the same.
